Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed so we keep momentum:

Summary of requirements you outlined on the call:
- PII filtering and ability to limit retention windows for user inputs and model outputs.
- Data residency: workload to remain within us-west region for the first phase.
- Encryption: in-transit and at-rest must meet your cryptography standards; customer-managed keys (BYOK) required for production.
- Auditability: detailed access logs and key usage audit events retained for 1 year.

Action items I promised to follow up on:
1) Confirm supported TLS versions and whether mutual-TLS (mTLS) is available for private endpoints.
2) Clarify how CMK/BYOK works across our deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
3) Share our SOC 2 summary and a short doc on KMS/HSM integration options.
4) Propose next steps: technical deep-dive with your security team + our Security lead (Vivek), and a sample MAP for procurement.

Attached: redwood_kms_options.pdf (high-level), SOC2-summary.pdf. I've also drafted a mutual-action-plan spreadsheet to get procurement details (attached).

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifying points from our side before we schedule the deep-dive: 

- BYOK: we need confirmation that keys can be customer-managed and that key material never leaves our KMS/HSM. For hosted SaaS options we prefer an envelope encryption model where our KMS performs encryption/decryption and Redwood never has access to plaintext keys.
- HSM support: Can Redwood integrate with CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM, or do you only support standard KMS APIs? Our legal/security folks will want specifics on key wrapping and key escrow.
- Logs: the team asks for an example of the key usage audit events and whether those are exported to our SIEM (SPLUNK).
- Retention: If we set a 30-day retention policy for raw prompts and outputs, can you guarantee deletion and provide an attestation process?

Also, we're evaluating whether Dedicated or Private makes sense. Cost is a factor but so is the guarantee that cryptographic controls meet our compliance needs.

I'll sleep on availability — Wednesday afternoon PT should work for us.

Thanks,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Hi Daniel —

Following up with technical details (short version) based on Marissa's notes. Happy to take these deeper on the call.

Encryption (in-transit):
- We enforce TLS 1.2+ for all public endpoints and recommend TLS 1.3 where clients support it.
- Mutual TLS is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated endpoints behind customer-managed load balancers; for hosted API we support mTLS on customer-specific VPC endpoints.

Encryption (at-rest):
- All model weights, checkpoint artifacts, and customer data are encrypted at-rest using AES-256-GCM. We use envelope encryption by default.

Customer-managed keys (BYOK):
- Hosted API (standard): supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via supported cloud KMS APIs (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). In this mode, Redwood never stores raw key material; we use KMS to perform key wrapping/unwrapping operations.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): supports BYOK with KMS integration; you can configure key policies and have key usage audit logs forwarded to your cloud logging project.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full BYOK and HSM integration available — we can support HSMs that expose PKCS#11 (including CloudHSM and on-prem HSMs) and can also configure key-import workflows where required.

Key handling notes:
- We use envelope encryption with a data encryption key (DEK) per customer/tenant; DEKs are wrapped by your CMK. Redwood does not retain plaintext DEKs on disk.
- Key rotation: supported; you can rotate CMKs and we will re-wrap DEKs with the new CMK per your rotation schedule.
- No key escrow: we do not escrow customer key material.

Audit & logging:
- Key usage events (Encrypt/Decrypt/Wrap/Unwrap) are emitted as structured logs and can be exported to your SIEM via our logging integration (Cloud Logging / CloudWatch / forwarders).
- Access logs for API calls include token/user identifiers and the model route invoked; retention is configurable at the deployment layer.

Data retention / deletion:
- Retention policies are configurable per route/model. For Hosted we can apply tenant-level retention policies (e.g., 30 days) and provide deletion attestations on request. For Dedicated/Private you get direct controls and can configure automated purge jobs.
- Note on caches: ephemeral KV cache used for inference is not persisted across node replacements unless you explicitly enable persistent caching in Dedicated/Private (not enabled by default).

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (redacted), and redwood_kms_options.pdf with diagrams showing envelope flow and KMS integrations. I've also attached a short KB link in the MAP in case you want a pre-read.

If you like, we can run a short proof-of-concept on a sandbox dedicated instance to demonstrate BYOK and log forwarding.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
